connection_condition: atom.molecule_id corresponds to molecule.molecule_id; every atom row carries the identifier of its parent molecule
description: A molecule is composed of its atoms; an atom cannot exist without its parent molecule. 12333 atoms belong to 444 distinct molecule identifiers.

connection_condition: bond.molecule_id corresponds to molecule.molecule_id; every bond row carries the identifier of its parent molecule
description: A molecule is composed of its bonds; a bond cannot exist without its parent molecule. 12379 bonds belong to 444 distinct molecule identifiers.

connection_condition: connected.bond_id corresponds to bond.bond_id; each bond is expanded into exactly two directional connection rows
description: Every connection row is a directional component of one bond: a bond is represented by two connection records, one per direction, and a connection cannot exist without its bond.
A single bond is a kind of chemical bond; the set of bonds whose bond type is the single-bond symbol is a subset of all bonds (10528 of 12379).
A double bond is a kind of chemical bond; the set of bonds whose bond type is the double-bond symbol is a subset of all bonds (1844 of 12379).
A triple bond is a kind of chemical bond; the set of bonds whose bond type is the triple-bond symbol is a subset of all bonds (6 of 12379).
A carcinogenic molecule is a kind of molecule; molecules with a positive label form a subset of all molecules (152 of 343 labelled molecules).
A non-carcinogenic molecule is a kind of molecule; molecules with a negative label form a subset of all molecules (191 of 343 labelled molecules).
An unconnected atom is a kind of atom: it is the subset of atoms that have no connection row, a state-based rather than structural subtype (49 atoms).

connection_condition: atom.element carries the element symbol of each atom row; there is no separate element table and no element identifier column
description: Each atom is classified by exactly one chemical element through an attribute value on the atom row rather than through a type hierarchy, so the connection is an attribute association.

connection_condition: connected.atom_id and connected.atom_id2 each correspond to atom.atom_id; both atoms of a connection belong to the same molecule
description: A connection relates two atoms of one molecule; the atoms are referenced by their atom identifiers, and the connection carries no meaning without both endpoints.

connection_condition: connected.bond_id and bond.bond_id share the same identifier domain, verified by sampling; the connected table holds exactly two rows per bond_id, one per direction
description: In the workload, 'connection' and 'bond' name the same underlying entity and questions use the two words interchangeably; they differ only in multiplicity, since a bond is represented by two directional connection rows, so a total bond count must not be taken from raw connection rows.
The atom index is derived from atom_id: it is the numeric suffix that follows the molecule identifier and the underscore separator.
The atom count of a molecule is derived by counting the atom rows that carry that molecule identifier.
The bond count of a molecule is derived by counting the bond rows that carry that molecule identifier.
The element percentage is derived from the element classification of atoms and the size of the reference atom set, as the count of atoms of that element divided by the total atoms in the set.
The bond type percentage is derived from the bond type classification of bonds and the size of the reference bond set, as the count of bonds of that type divided by the total bonds in the set.

connection_condition: indirect: bond.molecule_id corresponds to molecule.molecule_id, so bond types are comparable between carcinogenic and non-carcinogenic molecules; there is no direct column connecting the two concepts
description: Workload analyses cross carcinogenicity with bond type distribution, for example triple-bonded carcinogenic molecules; the two concepts meet only through the shared molecule identifier.
